title: How far apart are Manipur and Rajasthan?
description: Manipur at about plus one hundred and Rajasthan at about minus ninety three are compared on the rice and wheat scale. The video finds the distance as one hundred minus minus ninety three, and breaks Keeko's doubt that the gap is seven.
teaching_notes: One idea: the distance between a positive value and a negative value is found by subtracting the smaller from the larger. Watch for students who subtract the sizes ignoring the signs.

source: Manipur is about +100 and Rajasthan about -93. How far apart
video_script.why: The child can read single values on the scale and now finds the distance between two states on opposite sides of zero.
video_script.substitution: Subtract the smaller value from the larger value, taking care of the minus sign.
video_script.anchor: the book's rice and wheat scale with Manipur near the rice end and Rajasthan near the wheat end
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes ninety three from one hundred and ignores that Rajasthan is on the other side of zero.
video_script.payoff_line: manipur and rajasthan are one hundred ninety three steps apart

final_answer.value: 193 steps apart; rainfall data could help explain the gap
final_answer.spoken: manipur and rajasthan are one hundred ninety three steps apart, and rainfall data could help explain the gap

maths_rules: Manipur is about +100 and Rajasthan about -93 on a scale from -100 to +100
distance = larger value - smaller value = 100 - (-93) = 100 + 93 = 193 steps
the whole scale is 200 steps, so the two states are almost at opposite ends
rainfall data for the two states could help explain the gap, since rice needs much more water
slip: 100 - 93 = 7 treats both values as being on the same side of zero
video_script.design: One idea: cross zero, so add the two distances from zero. The wrong idea is subtracting the sizes. A number line from minus one hundred to plus one hundred stays on screen all video.
